Specifically verify or refute this candidate finding, stated here as a claim to check, not as settled: letflow_queue/tasks/task.ex line 18 defines @statuses ~w(open done blocked) -- i.e. 'blocked' is ALREADY a legal release_lock status today, and tasks.ex's get_next_task/1 SQL eligibility predicate filters on t.status = 'open' only, meaning a task released with status:blocked is ALREADY excluded from future get_next_task claims. Also verify: tap_maybe_close_github_issue/2 only fires on status == "done" (see tasks.ex ~line 382-399), so releasing with status:blocked does NOT best-effort-close the GitHub issue. If both of these check out, the LIFO re-selection HAZARD described in ISS-0459 may already be preventable today by releasing with status:"blocked" instead of status:"done" or no-status -- state plainly whether this is true, and if so, why TASK_QUEUE.md's own text (as quoted in ISS-0459's own description, and as you should re-read directly) does not already document this as the answer. Consider: does 'blocked' as an English word semantically mismatched the instrumented/no_defect meaning badly enough that documenting it under that name would misinform a future reader, even if it is mechanically sufficient? Give your own reasoned judgment, do not just report symptom.
3. State plainly: does ANY existing letflow-queue status value, or ANY existing TASK_QUEUE.md-documented mechanism, already fully satisfy ISS-0459's Acceptance Criterion 1 (a release_lock status/mechanism that marks a task terminally closed for LIFO-selection purposes without asserting resolved and without best-effort-closing an already-closed GitHub issue)? Your answer drives whether CODE-DESIGNER's next step is 'add a new status value + migration' or 'document existing blocked semantics correctly, no code change' or something else.
4. Do NOT implement anything. Do NOT edit letflow-queue's source. Do NOT edit TASK_QUEUE.md or ISSUE_QUEUE.md yet -- that is CODE-DESIGNER's and then ELIXIR-DEV's job, after a design gate.
5. Write your diagnosis into result.summary: root cause (confirmed or refuted against source), the 'blocked' finding's verdict, and what a fix needs to change (or confirm needs no code change, only docs).
